aiSummary: Speckled trout are the most consistent target across Choctawhatchee Bay right now, with redfish and flounder also showing up on bay trips — the bite is improving daily after a stretch of rough conditions. Today's heat index will push to 106°F, so an early morning departure is essential; fish your best water before the sun gets high and the heat sets in. A 14% storm chance exists before 1 PM, so keep an eye on the western sky and plan to be off exposed water by midday.

bridge.aiNote: The 331 Bridge spans the narrow neck of Choctawhatchee Bay, creating a current funnel that pushes bait through on both tides and concentrates speckled trout, redfish, sheepshead, and black drum around the pilings year-round. The lee-side pilings are the prime ambush zone on incoming tides, as fish stack up to intercept bait moving through the funnel. Keep in mind this is open, exposed water — it's typically the first spot to become unfishable when wind picks up.
bridge.todaysCall: Today's west wind at 0–10 mph is light enough to keep the bridge fishable, but get there early — the strong waxing gibbous tidal push means current will be moving well even as the tide drops toward the 2:39 PM low. Work the lee-side pilings during the morning outgoing tide; slightly stained water favors darker or chartreuse soft plastics and suspending plugs worked tight to the structure. The incoming tide ran through the predawn hours, so by sunrise the tide will be falling — position on the downcurrent side of the pilings and let your presentation sweep naturally. With the slim storm window before 1 PM and exposed conditions here, plan to wrap up or relocate well before noon.

alaqua.aiNote: Alaqua Bayou offers protected water with a strong year-round redfish population, along with trout and flounder at the mouth. The oyster bars at the creek mouth are the prime target zone, while tree cover keeps interior water a few degrees cooler than the open bay and provides shelter from wind and weather. The upper creek transitions to brackish water where bass join the mix alongside smaller reds.
alaqua.todaysCall: The tree-lined banks and protected layout make Alaqua a smart choice on a scorching day like today — that shade buffer is meaningful when the heat index is pushing 106°F, so work the shaded, cooler stretches of the upper creek during the midmorning hours. The tide is falling toward a 2:39 PM low, so focus the early morning on the oyster bars at the creek mouth while there's still enough water to hold fish; as the tide drops, reds will push up into the grass edges and creek bends. Slightly stained water calls for louder, more visible presentations — a gold spoon, weedless paddle tail in a dark color, or popping cork over the oyster bars are all good options. Flounder have been showing on bay trips this week, so don't overlook the creek mouth with a slow-dragged jig on or near the bottom.

basin.aiNote: Basin Bayou sees less fishing pressure than neighboring spots, which typically means less-educated fish willing to bite. The interior grass flats are classic sight-fishing territory for redfish in under two feet of water, and pompano occasionally show at the mouth on moving tides in late spring and early summer. It offers a quieter experience but is less protected than LaGrange when weather starts to build.
basin.todaysCall: Lower pressure here makes Basin worth a look, especially for sight-fishing reds on the interior grass flats during the first couple hours of daylight when the sun angle is low enough to spot fish without spooking them. The falling tide this morning will concentrate reds on the flat edges and drain points — pole or drift quietly and look for wakes or tailing fish in the skinny water. Slightly stained clarity means you may need to get a bit closer than ideal for sight-fishing, so move slow and keep the trolling motor noise minimal. With the storm window closing before 1 PM and Basin offering less weather protection than LaGrange, keep your exit plan in mind and don't push your luck if clouds start building to the west.

lagrange.aiNote: LaGrange Bayou is widely regarded as the top trout producer in this part of the bay, with legendary oyster bars at the mouth and interior grass flats that hold redfish year-round. Deep holes inside the bayou hold black drum and sheepshead, and the overall layout is the most protected water on this side of the bay. When weather builds, LaGrange is the go-to refuge on this stretch.
lagrange.todaysCall: LaGrange is an excellent call today — it's the most protected spot on this side of the bay if that sub-1 PM storm chance materializes, and the oyster bars at the mouth will be firing during the morning outgoing tide ahead of the 2:39 PM low. Speckled trout are the top producer across the bay right now, and the mouth bars here are prime early-morning trout water; work topwaters or suspending plugs over and around the shell in the low-light window right after the 5:57 AM sunrise. As the tide drops, shift inside to the grass flats and target reds in the draining water; the strong spring-tide pull from the waxing gibbous moon means more pronounced water movement and better bait concentration than a typical summer day. Slightly stained water suits this spot well — natural-colored soft plastics and gold spoons both work, and the deeper interior holes are worth a drop for black drum if the flat bite slows.

fourmile.aiNote: Four Mile Creek is a tidal creek running between Shipyard Marina and the bay, making it one of the most convenient launches on the water. Incoming tides push baitfish up the creek, concentrating redfish and trout in the bends and grass edges, while the creek mouth is a reliable flounder zone. The upper section transitions to brackish water where bass appear alongside smaller reds, and the short, enclosed layout makes it the safest fishery when weather threatens.
fourmile.todaysCall: Four Mile is your safety net today — if that early storm chance pops before 1 PM, this enclosed creek is where you want to be. The tide was incoming through the predawn hours and is now falling toward the afternoon low, so fish the bends and grass edges where reds and trout stacked up on the overnight push; they'll be holding tight as water drains back out. Flounder have been reported on bay trips this week, so work a slow jig or live finger mullet along the bottom near the creek mouth early. The light west wind at 0–10 mph won't factor in here at all given the creek's protection, making for comfortable, fishable conditions throughout the morning.

hogtown.aiNote: Hogtown Bayou is a signature Santa Rosa Beach guide destination and one of the most productive trout flats on the bay. Summer mornings are the peak window, with trout stacked on grass flats in two to four feet of water, and Spanish mackerel show at the mouth on moving tides. It sees regular pressure from local guides, but produces consistently enough to remain a top pick despite the traffic.
hogtown.todaysCall: Hogtown is a natural fit today — guide reports from this week specifically highlight the Santa Rosa Beach and Choctawhatchee Bay area as producing solid trout numbers with quality fish mixed in, and summer mornings on the grass flats here are the peak window for exactly that. Hit the 2–4 foot grass zone right at sunrise (5:57 AM) and work it hard through the early outgoing tide; the strong spring-tide current from the nearly full moon will keep bait moving and trout active. Slightly stained water means a noisy topwater or a chartreuse/white paddle tail under a popping cork will outperform finesse presentations in low light. Factor in the extra run time from Shipyard Marina compared to the bayous closer to the 331 bridge, and be heading back or tucked into protected water before the pre-1 PM storm window opens.

rocky.aiNote: Rocky Bayou sits inside Fred Gannon Rocky Bayou State Park near Niceville, offering protected, scenic water that sees significantly less pressure than the bayous closer to the 331 bridge. Freshwater influence from Rocky Creek makes flounder fishing excellent, and the glass-calm state park coves are ideal for sight-fishing redfish. Mangrove snapper hold near dock pilings, rounding out a diverse and underutilized fishery.
rocky.todaysCall: Rocky Bayou's low pressure and glass-calm coves make it a rewarding destination on a bright, sunny summer day — sight-fishing for reds in the clear state park shallows is at its best in early morning before the sun gets high and fish go deep into the shade. The 85°F water and bright sun will push fish tight to shaded structure and deeper edges by mid-morning, so prioritize the sight-fishing window in the first 90 minutes after the 5:57 AM sunrise. Mangrove snapper near the dock pilings are a great secondary target as the heat climbs — small jigs or live shrimp fished tight to the structure will get bit. Rocky is the furthest run from Shipyard Marina, so plan your departure accordingly and keep the pre-1 PM storm window in mind when deciding when to head back.
